The company’s refining arm reached a record utilization factor of 101.2% in the quarter, boosting oil products output by 5.6% over the prior period while maintaining a 68% yield of higher value-added fuels such as diesel, jet fuel, and gasoline. Overall sales revenues climbed nearly 43% from the first quarter and almost 60% year-on-year, while free cash flow almost doubled versus 1Q26 to about US$7.7 billion, and return on capital employed improved to 9.3%, reflecting both operational efficiency gains and a more favorable pricing environment.

NRX Pharmaceuticals ( (NRXP) ) has shared an update.

NRx Pharmaceuticals said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration completed a first-round review of its Abbreviated New Drug Application for preservative-free ketamine, filed in September 2025, and on July 30, 2026 reported no major deficiencies related to the drug itself. The agency instead raised a single major deficiency concerning the twist-off cap of the luer lock vial, seeking assurance that potential deformation of the vial tip would not compromise patient safety.

To address the packaging issue, NRx noted that the same luer lock vial has been used in three previously approved ANDA products, with 11.9 million doses shipped in the past 12 months without complaints or recalls, and provided testing data on 3,500 vials and independent torque verification. At a clarification meeting on August 6, 2026, the FDA requested formal certifications from manufacturers confirming that the ketamine product is made on the same lines and with the same materials as those approved products.

NRx said this information, already contained in the application, will now be resubmitted as signed certifications, after which the FDA committed to immediately restart its review to resolve the packaging concern in the shortest possible cycle. The meeting included leadership from the Office of Generic Drugs and the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, which acknowledged ketamine’s status as a strategic medicine on the federal drug shortage list.

Management characterized the outcome of the first-round review as positive, emphasizing that few ANDAs clear this stage without drug-related major deficiencies. The company indicated it remains optimistic that the packaging issue can be resolved in time to enable initial commercial sales in 2026, aligning with federal recognition of a ketamine shortage and the lack of U.S.-based supply, which could bolster NRx’s position in this critical market segment.
